turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good morning. Kindly sit, I will check the vitals before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Good morning. The rain slowed the traffic quite a bit, I hope we have not delayed you.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not to worry. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Pulse is eighty-eight, oh wait, sorry, the probe slipped, it is seventy-eight.

[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is thirty-six point six, saturation ninety-eight percent, respiratory rate sixteen per minute. Weight today is sixty-two kilograms. Last time in March you were fifty-eight, and your last pressure was one-thirty over eighty-four.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, sister.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): May I come in as well? I am his mother.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, please, both of you. I am Dr. Mehta. So, what brings you in?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I have a lump on the left side of my neck. That is why I have come, actually. It has been there for three weeks.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He told me it was nothing only, but I said kindly show it to a doctor.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): You did the right thing. Is the lump paining?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It is not painful, even if I press on it.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hmm, painless, alright. Any fever nowadays?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sweating in the night?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Only once, doctor. About ten days back, um, I woke up and the shirt was damp. After that it has not happened.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sore throat?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss with this?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Never.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I should also mention, doctor, I have asthma since childhood. It is under control. I use the purple inhaler, two puffs in the morning and two at night, though the brand name is not coming to me, I am sorry.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): No issue, we will call it the purple inhaler for the moment. Do you take any other medicine?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Only crocine, uh, Crocin. Five hundred milligrams, by mouth, if I have a headache. Maybe once in a month.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None that I am aware of.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Our cat scratched his right hand, sometime last month. Small scratch, it healed.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is right. She scratched my right hand about a month ago. It healed by itself. There is nothing there now.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not take alcohol, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): What is your work?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a junior accountant in a private firm. I stay with my parents.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, before I forget, did you catch the match last night? India were in trouble till the end.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): I only saw the highlights while having tea. That last over, umm, I did not expect it.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): We were talking about it in the auto itself. The driver had the radio on full.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the rain, my god. The lane behind our house is like a small river since yesterday evening.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): The tea shop downstairs was closed also. Mother wanted filter coffee and she is still a little upset about it.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am not upset. I am only saying one cup would have been nice. The corporation drain is blocked again, that is the real problem.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ha, the monsoon routine. Right. Let me return to the medical side, if you do not mind.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): With the asthma, are you wheezing these days?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. When the dust is more I get a little wheeze. Not every day.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain along with it?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the stomach side, motions, appetite, any problem?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. All that is normal.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let me examine the neck. Please look up a bit.

[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): I can feel a soft lump on the left side of the neck, about two centimetres, it is mobile and not tender. No other nodes in the neck or in the axilla. The throat is clear. The chest is clear, no wheeze just now.

[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Err, so putting it together. A painless lump for three weeks, one night of sweating, no fever now, longstanding asthma, and a cat scratch last month that has healed. My working impression is a reactive lymph node, possibly from the scratch. I also cannot rule out a lymphoma, so that remains a possibility till the reports come.

[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am booking blood tests today, a full blood count and an ESR, and an ultrasound of the neck. Please continue the purple inhaler as usual. Kindly do not keep pressing the lump. If there is high fever or the lump grows quickly, come earlier, otherwise I will see you in two weeks with the reports.
[SEG0052] person_1 (NURSE): I will hand you the lab form. Blood collection is the second door on the left, after you step out.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you very much, doctor. We will be back in two weeks.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We should leave before the rain starts again. Thank you.

spec.situation: Young adult with a painless neck lump for three weeks, night sweats once, no fever now; recent cat scratch mentioned; doctor examines and orders blood tests and ultrasound.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
